lab.name: Laboratory on Polymer Materials & Organ Printing
lab.tagline: Functional polymer materials — from hydrogels and bioinspired fibres to bioprinted tissues.

about: Dr. Anayancy Osorio-Madrazo leads the Laboratory on Polymer Materials & Organ Printing at the University of Bayreuth.

Before joining Bayreuth, she built her independent research group at the University of Freiburg in 2016, for which she was awarded both an Emmy Noether Programme junior group grant of the German Research Foundation (DFG) and a Margarete von Wrangell Habilitation Programme grant from Ministry of Science, Research and Arts (MWK) Baden-Württemberg.

Her research bridges polymer chemistry, materials science, physics, engineering and biomedicine — with a focus on synthesis, processing and structure–function relationship in soft matter — covering fundamental and applied research.

mission: Our group strives to develop functional polymer materials for the most diverse applications, covering fundamental and applied research for technological and biomedical ends.

We focus on design, chemistry, processing, characterization and application of polymer-based materials. For example, we utilize 3D printing technologies for the fabrication of functional tissues and organs and investigate their hierarchical structure and functionalities in relation to material processing and polymer chemistry.

Inspired by nature, the group develops new micro/nano-structured biomaterials of different morphologies for tissue engineering — bridging the gap between polymer science for achieving controlled fine microstructures and materials functionality and their targeted application.

team.name: Anayancy Osorio Madrazo
team.bio: Dr. Anayancy Osorio-Madrazo leads the Laboratory of Organ Printing at the University of Bayreuth since 2024. She led the Laboratory of Intelligent Polymer Materials at the University of Jena, have led the Emmy Noether junior research group funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) since 2021 (previously at the University of Freiburg). Besides, she was a fellow of the Margarete von Wrangell Habilitation programme for women, and a postdoctoral fellow of the Max Planck Society, Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces MPIKG. She is Secretary General of the European Chitin Society EUCHIS (www.euchis.org).

team.name: Ingo Dönch
team.bio: Dr. Ingo Dönch studied chemistry at the Freie Universität FU Berlin with a focus on polymer chemistry, completing his Diplom in 2004 on AFM of polyelectrolyte multilayers at the Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces (MPIKG). From 2004 to 2009 he did his doctorate at MPIKG on the mechanical properties of polyelectrolyte multilayers, working extensively with atomic force microscopy and neutron reflectometry. As a postdoc he worked on corrosion protection via sol-gel coatings and self-healing lacquers, then gained industry experience in personnel, lab management, business development and patents. Since 2017 he has worked as a postdoc on bioinspired biomaterials, 3D cell printing, culture and cell-culture monitoring at IMTEK, University of Freiburg, and more recently at the Laboratory of Organ Printing, University of Bayreuth.
